items.good: The girl who sits next to me is my cousin.
items.ko: 내 옆에 앉아 있는 소녀는 내 사촌이에요.
bad: The girl which sits next to me is my cousin.
The girl who sit next to me is my cousin.
The girl who she sits next to me is my cousin.

cz.st: The girl ___ sits next to me is my cousin.

items.rule: 선행사가 사람이고 관계절에서 주어 역할을 하면 주격 관계대명사 who를 써요. 관계대명사가 이미 주어이므로 she를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: I lost the book which my aunt gave me.
bad: I lost the book who my aunt gave me.
I lost the book which my aunt gave it to me.
I lost the book what my aunt gave me.

cz.st: I lost the book ___ my aunt gave me.

items.rule: 선행사가 사물이면 which를 써요. 관계대명사가 목적어 역할을 하므로 it을 다시 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: I know a boy whose father is a pilot.
bad: I know a boy who father is a pilot.
I know a boy whose his father is a pilot.
I know a boy which father is a pilot.

cz.st: I know a boy ___ father is a pilot.

items.rule: 소유를 나타낼 때는 whose를 써요. whose는 his 같은 소유격을 대신하므로 뒤에 his를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Everything that she said was true.
bad: Everything what she said was true.
Everything who she said was true.
Everything she said it was true.

cz.st: Everything ___ she said was true.

items.rule: everything, all, only 같은 말이 선행사일 때는 주로 that을 써요. 선행사가 이미 있으므로 what은 쓸 수 없어요.

items.good: This is the best movie that I have ever seen.
items.ko: 이것은 내가 지금까지 본 최고의 영화예요.
bad: This is the best movie what I have ever seen.
This is the best movie who I have ever seen.
This is the best movie that I have ever seen it.

cz.st: This is the best movie ___ I have ever seen.

items.rule: 최상급이 포함된 선행사 뒤에는 관계대명사 that을 즐겨 써요.

items.good: The teacher whom we respect retired last year.
bad: The teacher whose we respect retired last year.
The teacher whom we respect him retired last year.
The teacher which we respect retired last year.

cz.st: The teacher ___ we respect retired last year.

items.rule: 선행사가 사람이고 관계절에서 목적어 역할을 하면 목적격 whom을 써요. 사람에게 which는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The girl with whom I danced was Mina.
bad: The girl with who I danced was Mina.
The girl whom with I danced was Mina.
The girl with that I danced was Mina.

cz.st: The girl with ___ I danced was Mina.

items.rule: 전치사 바로 뒤에는 who나 that을 쓸 수 없고 사람이면 whom을 써요.

items.good: This is the house in which my grandfather was born.
bad: This is the house in that my grandfather was born.
This is the house which in my grandfather was born.
This is the house in who my grandfather was born.

cz.st: This is the house in ___ my grandfather was born.

items.rule: ‘전치사 + 관계대명사’에서 사물이면 which를 써요. 전치사 바로 뒤에는 that을 쓰지 못해요.

items.good: The song that I was listening to is my favorite.
items.ko: 내가 듣고 있던 노래는 내가 가장 좋아하는 곡이에요.
bad: The song that I was listening is my favorite.
The song what I was listening to is my favorite.
The song who I was listening to is my favorite.

cz.st: The song that I was listening ___ is my favorite.

items.rule: 전치사를 관계절 끝에 남겨 두면 그 전치사(listen to)를 빠뜨리면 안 돼요.

items.good: This is the park where we first met.
bad: This is the park which we first met.
This is the park who we first met.
This is the park where we first met there.

cz.st: This is the park ___ we first met.

items.rule: 장소를 나타내는 선행사 뒤에서 ‘in/at + 장소’의 뜻을 대신하면 관계부사 where를 써요. where 뒤에는 there를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: I remember the day when we won the game.
items.ko: 나는 우리가 경기에서 이겼던 날을 기억해요.
bad: I remember the day where we won the game.
I remember the day who we won the game.
I remember the day which we won the game.

cz.st: I remember the day ___ we won the game.

items.rule: 시간을 나타내는 선행사(day, time, year) 뒤에는 관계부사 when을 써요.

items.good: Tell me the reason why you are late.
bad: Tell me the reason when you are late.
Tell me the reason where you are late.
Tell me the reason who you are late.

cz.st: Tell me the reason ___ you are late.

items.rule: 이유를 나타내는 reason 뒤에는 관계부사 why를 써요.

items.good: My bike, which I bought last year, is already broken.
items.ko: 내 자전거는 작년에 샀는데 벌써 고장 났어요.
bad: My bike, that I bought last year, is already broken.
My bike, who I bought last year, is already broken.
My bike, which I bought it last year, is already broken.

cz.st: My bike, ___ I bought last year, is already broken.

items.rule: 쉼표 뒤에서 덧붙여 설명하는 관계절(계속적 용법)에는 that을 쓰지 않아요. 사물이므로 which를 써요.

items.good: My uncle, who lives in Busan, is a chef.
bad: My uncle, that lives in Busan, is a chef.
My uncle, which lives in Busan, is a chef.
My uncle, who live in Busan, is a chef.

cz.st: My uncle, ___ lives in Busan, is a chef.

items.rule: 쉼표를 쓰는 관계절에서는 that을 쓰지 않아요. 사람이므로 who를 쓰고, 동사는 선행사(단수)에 맞춰 lives로 써요.

items.good: The books that are on the desk belong to Jisu.
items.ko: 책상 위에 있는 책들은 지수의 것이에요.
bad: The books that is on the desk belong to Jisu.
The books that are on the desk belongs to Jisu.
The books what are on the desk belong to Jisu.

cz.st: The books that ___ on the desk belong to Jisu.

items.rule: 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 동사는 선행사의 수에 맞춰요. books가 복수이므로 are를 써요.

items.good: I live in a town whose streets are very narrow.
items.ko: 나는 길이 매우 좁은 마을에 살아요.
bad: I live in a town who streets are very narrow.
I live in a town which streets are very narrow.
I live in a town whose the streets are very narrow.

cz.st: I live in a town ___ streets are very narrow.

items.rule: whose는 사람뿐 아니라 사물의 소유 관계에도 쓰고, 바로 뒤에 관사 없이 명사가 와요.

items.good: The man who is talking to Mr. Kim is our new coach.
items.ko: 김 선생님과 이야기하고 있는 남자는 우리의 새 코치예요.
bad: The man who talking to Mr. Kim is our new coach.
The man whose is talking to Mr. Kim is our new coach.
The man who is talk to Mr. Kim is our new coach.

cz.st: The man who ___ talking to Mr. Kim is our new coach.

items.rule: 주격 관계대명사 뒤에는 동사가 와요. 진행형에서 be동사를 빠뜨리면 안 돼요.

items.good: He is the only student that passed the test.
bad: He is the only student what passed the test.
He is the only student whose passed the test.
He is the only student that he passed the test.

cz.st: He is the only student ___ passed the test.

items.rule: the only가 붙은 선행사 뒤에는 that을 즐겨 써요. that이 주어 역할을 하므로 he를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: What I need is a good night's sleep.
bad: That I need is a good night's sleep.
Which I need is a good night's sleep.
Who I need is a good night's sleep.

cz.st: ___ I need is a good night's sleep.

items.rule: 선행사 없이 ‘~하는 것’이라는 뜻의 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사는 what이에요.

items.good: I didn't understand what he said.
items.ko: 나는 그가 말한 것을 이해하지 못했어요.
bad: I didn't understand that he said.
I didn't understand who he said.
I didn't understand whose he said.

cz.st: I didn't understand ___ he said.

items.rule: ‘~하는 것’을 뜻하고 said의 목적어 역할을 하는 말은 what이에요.

items.good: All that I want is a quiet room.
bad: All what I want is a quiet room.
All who I want is a quiet room.
All that I want are a quiet room.

cz.st: All ___ I want is a quiet room.

items.rule: all 뒤의 관계대명사는 that을 써요. what은 이미 선행사 all이 있으면 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: He passed the exam, which made his parents happy.
items.ko: 그는 시험에 합격했고, 그것이 부모님을 기쁘게 했어요.
bad: He passed the exam, that made his parents happy.
He passed the exam, who made his parents happy.
He passed the exam, what made his parents happy.

cz.st: He passed the exam, ___ made his parents happy.

items.rule: which는 앞 문장 전체를 받아 ‘그것이 ~했다’는 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요. 쉼표 뒤에는 that을 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The movie that we watched yesterday was boring.
bad: The movie that we watched it yesterday was boring.
The movie who we watched yesterday was boring.
The movie what we watched yesterday was boring.

cz.st: The movie ___ we watched yesterday was boring.

items.rule: 목적격 관계대명사는 관계절 안에서 목적어 역할을 하므로 it 같은 목적어를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Mr. Han, whose son is my classmate, teaches music.
items.ko: 아들이 내 반 친구인 한 선생님은 음악을 가르쳐요.
bad: Mr. Han, who son is my classmate, teaches music.
Mr. Han, whose his son is my classmate, teaches music.
Mr. Han, which son is my classmate, teaches music.

cz.st: Mr. Han, ___ son is my classmate, teaches music.

items.rule: 소유격 관계대명사 whose 뒤에는 바로 명사(son)가 와요. 쉼표는 덧붙이는 설명이에요.

items.good: Ms. Lee, whom everyone admires, won the prize.
items.ko: 모두가 존경하는 이 선생님이 상을 받았어요.
bad: Ms. Lee, that everyone admires, won the prize.
Ms. Lee, whom everyone admires her, won the prize.
Ms. Lee, which everyone admires, won the prize.

cz.st: Ms. Lee, ___ everyone admires, won the prize.

items.rule: 쉼표 뒤 관계절에서 사람이 목적어이면 whom을 써요. that은 쓰지 않고, 사람에게 which는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Anyone who wants to join the club should sign up.
items.ko: 동아리에 들어오고 싶은 사람은 누구든 신청해야 해요.
bad: Anyone which wants to join the club should sign up.
Anyone who want to join the club should sign up.
Anyone whose wants to join the club should sign up.

cz.st: Anyone ___ wants to join the club should sign up.

items.rule: anyone은 사람을 가리키므로 who를 쓰고, 단수 취급하여 wants로 써요.

items.good: Those who work hard will succeed.
bad: Those which work hard will succeed.
Those who works hard will succeed.
Those who work hard will succeeds.

cz.st: Those ___ work hard will succeed.

items.rule: ‘those who ~’는 ‘~하는 사람들’이라는 뜻이고, 복수이므로 work로 써요.

items.good: The thing that surprised me most was the price.
items.ko: 나를 가장 놀라게 한 것은 가격이었어요.
bad: The thing what surprised me most was the price.
The thing who surprised me most was the price.
The thing that surprised me most were the price.

cz.st: The thing ___ surprised me most was the price.

items.rule: thing 같은 사물 선행사 뒤에서는 that을 쓸 수 있어요. what은 선행사와 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: We adopted a dog which was found on the street.
bad: We adopted a dog which found on the street.
We adopted a dog which it was found on the street.
We adopted a dog what was found on the street.

cz.st: We adopted a dog ___ was found on the street.

items.rule: 주격 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 바로 동사(was found)가 와요. 주어 it을 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
bad: The man who car was stolen called the police.
The man whose his car was stolen called the police.
The man whom car was stolen called the police.

cz.st: The man ___ car was stolen called the police.

items.rule: ‘그 남자의 차’라는 소유 관계이므로 whose를 써요.

items.good: The doctor who treated my grandmother was very kind.
items.ko: 할머니를 치료해 주신 의사 선생님은 아주 친절했어요.
bad: The doctor which treated my grandmother was very kind.
The doctor who treated her my grandmother was very kind.
The doctor who treated my grandmother were very kind.

cz.st: The doctor ___ treated my grandmother was very kind.

items.rule: 사람 선행사의 주격 관계대명사는 who예요. 전체 문장의 동사는 doctor(단수)에 맞춰 was를 써요.

items.good: I like people who are honest.
bad: I like people who is honest.
I like people which are honest.
I like people who they are honest.

cz.st: I like people who ___ honest.

items.rule: 관계대명사절의 동사는 선행사 people(복수)에 맞춰 are를 써요.

items.good: The pen with which she wrote is mine.
items.ko: 그녀가 그것으로 글씨를 쓴 펜은 내 거예요.
bad: The pen with that she wrote is mine.
The pen which with she wrote is mine.
The pen with who she wrote is mine.

cz.st: The pen with ___ she wrote is mine.

items.rule: 전치사 뒤의 관계대명사는 사물이면 which예요. that과 what은 쓸 수 없어요.

items.good: He is the man about whom everyone is talking.
bad: He is the man about who everyone is talking.
He is the man about that everyone is talking.
He is the man whom about everyone is talking.

cz.st: He is the man about ___ everyone is talking.

items.rule: 전치사 뒤에 사람 목적격이 오면 whom을 써요.

items.good: The village where she was born is very small.
bad: The village which she was born is very small.
The village where she was born in is very small.
The village who she was born is very small.

cz.st: The village ___ she was born is very small.

items.rule: ‘in the village’의 뜻을 대신하면 where를 써요. which를 쓰려면 in이 필요해요.

items.good: My grandmother lives in a house which has a big garden.
items.ko: 할머니는 큰 정원이 있는 집에 살고 계세요.
bad: My grandmother lives in a house who has a big garden.
My grandmother lives in a house whose has a big garden.
My grandmother lives in a house what has a big garden.

cz.st: My grandmother lives in a house ___ has a big garden.

items.rule: 사물 선행사의 주격 관계대명사는 which예요.

items.good: The teacher told us a story that made us laugh.
items.ko: 선생님은 우리를 웃게 한 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
bad: The teacher told us a story who made us laugh.
The teacher told us a story that it made us laugh.
The teacher told us a story what made us laugh.

cz.st: The teacher told us a story ___ made us laugh.

items.rule: 주격 관계대명사 that은 사람과 사물에 모두 쓸 수 있어요. what은 선행사 뒤에 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The woman I met yesterday works at the library.
items.ko: 내가 어제 만난 여자는 도서관에서 일해요.
bad: The woman I met her yesterday works at the library.
The woman met I yesterday works at the library.
The woman I met yesterday work at the library.

cz.st: The woman I met yesterday ___ at the library.

items.rule: 목적격 관계대명사는 생략할 수 있어요. 생략되어도 전체 문장의 동사는 woman(단수)에 맞춰 works로 써요.

items.good: The movie we saw last night was scary.
bad: The movie we saw it last night was scary.
The movie saw we last night was scary.
The movie we saw last night were scary.

cz.st: The movie we saw last night ___ scary.

items.rule: 생략된 목적격 관계대명사 뒤에서도 관계절 안에 목적어를 다시 쓰지 않아요. 주절의 동사는 movie에 맞춰 was예요.

items.good: Everything I own is in this box.
items.ko: 내가 가진 모든 것이 이 상자 안에 있어요.
bad: Everything I own are in this box.
Everything I own it is in this box.
Everything own I is in this box.

cz.st: Everything I own ___ in this box.

items.rule: everything은 단수 취급해요. 목적격 관계대명사 that이 생략된 문장이에요.

items.good: I have a dog that likes swimming.
bad: I have a dog it likes swimming.
I have a dog that like swimming.
I have a dog what likes swimming.

cz.st: I have a dog ___ likes swimming.

items.rule: 두 문장을 이을 때 관계대명사가 주어 it을 대신해요. 선행사가 dog(단수)이므로 likes로 써요.

items.good: My sister, who is a nurse, works at night.
bad: My sister, that is a nurse, works at night.
My sister, which is a nurse, works at night.
My sister, who are a nurse, works at night.

cz.st: My sister, ___ is a nurse, works at night.

items.rule: 쉼표를 쓰는 관계절에는 that을 쓰지 않고, 사람이므로 which도 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The mountains which we climbed were covered with snow.
items.ko: 우리가 오른 산들은 눈으로 덮여 있었어요.
bad: The mountains which we climbed was covered with snow.
The mountains who we climbed were covered with snow.
The mountains which we climbed them were covered with snow.

cz.st: The mountains which we climbed ___ covered with snow.

items.rule: 주절의 동사는 선행사 mountains(복수)에 맞춰요.

items.good: This is the museum that opened last month.
bad: This is the museum who opened last month.
This is the museum that it opened last month.
This is the museum what opened last month.

cz.st: This is the museum ___ opened last month.

items.rule: 사물 선행사의 주격 관계대명사로 that을 쓸 수 있어요.

items.good: Is there a shop near here where I can buy a bike?
items.ko: 이 근처에 자전거를 살 수 있는 가게가 있나요?
bad: Is there a shop near here which I can buy a bike?
Is there a shop near here who I can buy a bike?
Is there a shop near here when I can buy a bike?

cz.st: Is there a shop near here ___ I can buy a bike?

items.rule: ‘그 가게에서’의 뜻을 대신하는 장소의 관계부사는 where예요.

items.good: Mina has a cousin who studies in London.
bad: Mina has a cousin which studies in London.
Mina has a cousin who study in London.
Mina has a cousin whose studies in London.

cz.st: Mina has a cousin ___ studies in London.

items.rule: 사람 선행사의 주격 관계대명사는 who이고, 동사는 선행사 cousin(단수)에 맞춰요.

items.good: The students who were late missed the bus.
bad: The students which were late missed the bus.
The students who was late missed the bus.
The students who were late missed the bus it.

cz.st: The students ___ were late missed the bus.

items.rule: 복수 선행사 the students 뒤에서도 사람이면 who를 써요.

items.good: The bag that she bought is expensive.
bad: The bag that she bought it is expensive.
The bag who she bought is expensive.
The bag what she bought is expensive.

cz.st: The bag ___ she bought is expensive.

items.rule: 사물 선행사의 목적격 관계대명사로 that을 쓸 수 있고, 관계절 안에 it을 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The man ___ lives next door is a dentist.
o: which
whose
who
what
items.why: 사람 선행사 the man이고 뒤에 바로 동사 lives가 오므로 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
She has a necklace ___ belonged to her grandmother.
o: who
which
whose
whom
items.why: 선행사 a necklace는 사물이고 뒤에 동사 belonged가 오므로 which가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
I met a girl ___ brother plays for the school team.
o: who
which
whom
whose
items.why: ‘그 소녀의 오빠’라는 소유 관계이고 뒤에 명사 brother가 오므로 whose예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
He is the boy ___ I told you about.
o: whose
whom
which
what
items.why: about의 목적어가 되는 사람이므로 목적격 whom이 알맞아요. 사람에게는 which를 쓰지 않아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
This is the most interesting book ___ I have read this year.
o: who
what
that
whose
items.why: 최상급이 있는 선행사 뒤에는 관계대명사 that을 즐겨 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Look at the birds ___ are flying over the lake.
o: whose

items.title: The Little Free Library
items.text: On Maple Street, there is a small wooden box that looks like a house. It is a little library which belongs to everyone in the neighborhood. People who have finished a book can leave it there, and anyone who wants something new to read can take one. The box was built by Mr. Park, whose grandchildren love stories. Last winter, he added a roof so that the books would stay dry when it snowed. Now children, parents, and even people who are just passing by stop to look. Mr. Park says the best part is meeting neighbors he had never talked to before.

items.title: A New Classmate
items.text: Last Monday, a new student named Haru joined our class. He is a boy who moved here from a small island. At first he was shy, but he soon became friends with Minseo, whose desk is next to his. During lunch, he taught us a game that children play on his island. The rule which surprised us most was that nobody is ever out. Our teacher, who watched us from the door, smiled and said that she wanted every class to have a day when students teach each other. We all agreed it was the best lunch of the week.

qs.why: who의 선행사는 바로 앞의 Our teacher예요.

qs.q: Why did the teacher smile?
o: She liked the idea of students teaching one another.
She was happy that the long lunch was finally over.
She wanted to join the game with the students herself.
She thought Haru had lost the game on purpose.
qs.why: 학생들이 서로 가르치는 날을 만들고 싶다고 말했으므로 그 생각이 마음에 든 거예요.

qs.q: The word “shy” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: excited about learning the new game rules
unable to understand what other people say
not comfortable talking to new people
tired after a long trip by boat
qs.why: At first ... shy, but he soon became friends라는 흐름에서 낯선 사람과 말하기 어려워하는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Bees at Work
items.text: Bees are insects that live in large groups called colonies. In each colony, there is one queen who lays the eggs. The workers, which are all female, collect flower juice and carry it back home. When a worker finds a field where many flowers grow, she dances to tell the others where to go. The honey that we eat is made from this juice. Without bees, many plants that give us fruit could not make seeds. That is the reason why scientists want to protect them.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How honey is sold in stores around the world
Why female workers are stronger than the queen
How bees live and why they are important
How scientists build homes for insects
qs.why: 벌의 생활 방식과 벌이 중요한 이유를 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does a worker’s dance tell the other bees?
o: When the queen is ready to lay more eggs
Which of the bees should make the honey today
Where a good field of flowers is
How many seeds each flower plant makes
qs.why: she dances to tell the others where to go라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence “The honey that we eat is made from this juice,” what does “that” refer to?
o: The queen
The honey
The juice
The field
qs.why: that의 선행사는 바로 앞의 The honey예요.

qs.q: What would probably happen if bees disappeared?
o: Queens would live in much larger colonies than before.
Workers would find many more fields of flowers.
Honey would become much easier for people to make.
Some fruit plants would have trouble making seeds.
qs.why: 벌이 없으면 과일을 맺는 많은 식물이 씨를 만들 수 없다고 했어요.

items.title: Grandfather’s Watch
items.text: My grandfather has an old watch that stopped working years ago. He never wears it, but he keeps it in a drawer where he also keeps old photos. Once I asked him why he did not throw it away. He told me that his own father, whose job was fixing trains, gave it to him when he was twenty. “A thing which holds a memory is never useless,” he said. Last week, I took the watch to a shop where a kind woman repaired it for free. When I gave it back, my grandfather’s eyes became wet, and he held my hand for a long time.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A watch that carries a special family memory
A shop where a kind woman repairs watches for free
A drawer in which a family keeps old photographs
A grandfather who spent his working life fixing trains
qs.why: 낡은 시계가 가족의 추억을 담고 있다는 내용이 중심이에요.

qs.q: Who gave the watch to Grandfather?
o: The woman at the shop
His grandson
His friend from school
His father
qs.why: his own father ... gave it to him이라고 했어요.

qs.q: The word “useless” in the passage means
o: worth keeping for many years
very expensive to buy in a shop
hard to find in a small town
not able to be used well
qs.why: use + less는 쓸모가 없다는 뜻이에요. 할아버지는 추억을 담은 물건은 쓸모없지 않다고 말했어요.

qs.q: Why did Grandfather’s eyes become wet?
o: He was sad that the shop closed.
He was angry that the writer took the watch.
He was moved to see the watch repaired.
He was tired after a long walk.
qs.why: 추억이 담긴 시계를 고쳐 오자 감동해서 눈이 젖고 손을 잡았다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence “a drawer where he also keeps old photos,” what does “where” refer to?
o: The drawer
The shop
The watch
The train
qs.why: where는 앞의 a drawer를 가리켜요.

items.title: The Night Market
items.text: A night market is a place where people go to eat, shop, and enjoy the evening. Stalls that sell hot snacks fill the street, and the smell of fried food reaches you before you see the first lamp. Vendors who work there every night know their regular customers by name. Tourists, whose first visit is often the most exciting, usually try something they have never eaten before. My cousin, who loves spicy food, once ate a dish which made him cry. Still, he laughed and ordered another. For many people, the market is not only a place to buy food but also a place where the city shows its character.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: A night market is a lively place that offers more than food.
Vendors should learn the names of every single customer who visits.
Spicy food is too dangerous for most of the tourists who come.
Cities should close their busy streets in the evening for safety.
qs.why: 음식뿐 아니라 도시의 분위기까지 보여 주는 활기찬 장소라는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What made the writer’s cousin cry?
o: A story told by a vendor
A very spicy dish
The smoke of a lamp
A sad ending to a visit
qs.why: a dish which made him cry에서 매운 음식 때문이라는 걸 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What can we say about the cousin?
o: He dislikes trying any kind of new food.
He cannot eat anything hot or spicy at all.
He likes bold flavors, even painful ones.
He never goes to night markets with his family.
qs.why: 울 정도였는데도 웃으며 하나 더 주문했으니 강한 맛을 즐기는 사람이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence “Vendors who work there every night know their regular customers by name,” “regular customers” are people who
o: visit a stall for the first time
come to the market again and again
sell food at the stalls
take photos of the lamps
qs.why: regular는 자주 오는 단골을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the sentence “Stalls that sell hot snacks fill the street,” “that” refers to
o: the street
the snacks
the evening
the stalls
qs.why: that의 선행사는 바로 앞의 Stalls예요.

items.title: A Robot Helper
items.text: Our school bought a robot that helps students in the library. It can find books which are hard to reach and carry them to a table. The students who use the robot say it is polite because it always says thank you. Mr. Choi, who is the librarian, explains that the robot cannot choose books for you. “It is a tool that saves time, not a teacher who knows your taste,” he says. He hopes that students will still ask people for advice, because a reader whose friends share books usually reads more.

qs.q: What is Mr. Choi’s attitude toward the robot?
o: He believes it should also teach younger students how to read.
He worries that the robot will take his job as a librarian one day.
He thinks it is useful but cannot replace people’s advice.
He wants to remove the robot from the library before this year ends.
qs.why: 도구로서는 유익하지만 사람의 조언을 대신할 수는 없다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can the robot do?
o: Choose the best book for each reader
Teach reading to young children
Repair broken books
Carry hard-to-reach books to a table
qs.why: find books which are hard to reach and carry them to a table이라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence “It is a tool that saves time,” “It” refers to
o: the library
the table
the librarian
the robot
qs.why: It은 앞에서 말한 robot을 가리켜요.

qs.q: The word “taste” in the passage means
o: the flavor of food
a kind of library rule
what a person likes
a sound in the library
qs.why: 책을 골라 줄 수 있는 선생님이 아니라는 문맥에서 사람의 취향을 뜻해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, who usually reads more?
o: A student who uses the robot every day
A reader whose friends share books
A librarian who has many books
A child who borrows only short books
qs.why: a reader whose friends share books usually reads more라고 했어요.

items.title: A Good Night’s Sleep
items.text: Doctors who study sleep say that teenagers need about nine hours every night. Students who stay up late often feel tired in class and find it difficult to remember things which they learned the day before. Experts suggest a routine that starts about an hour before bed. First, put away phones and tablets, whose bright screens can keep your brain awake. Then read a book or listen to quiet music that makes you calm. Finally, go to bed at the same time every day, even on weekends, because the body likes habits. A week later, many people who follow this advice say they wake up feeling happier.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why phones and tablets should be banned from schools
What kind of quiet music helps students study best
How teenagers can build a routine for better sleep
How many hours doctors need to sleep every day
qs.why: 십 대가 잘 자기 위한 습관을 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer suggest putting away phones and tablets?
o: Their bright screens keep the brain awake.
They are too expensive for students to keep.
They make the quiet music sound too loud.
They break more easily when used at night.
qs.why: whose bright screens can keep your brain awake라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which statement is true according to the passage?
o: The advice works only on weekdays.
Students who sleep late remember more.
Teenagers need about nine hours of sleep.
People feel worse after a week of the routine.
qs.why: teenagers need about nine hours every night라고 했어요.

qs.q: The word “routine” in the passage means
o: a quiet song with a slow and gentle beat
a short test that students take every week
a list of foods that people eat before bed
a set of things you do in the same order
qs.why: 잠자기 전에 매일 같은 순서로 하는 행동을 뜻해요.

items.title: The Recycling Club
items.text: Every Thursday, the Recycling Club meets in a classroom where old posters still hang on the walls. The members are students who care about the planet. Their latest project is a box that collects used batteries. Last month, they asked a shop owner whose store sells electronics to put a second box at his door. In two weeks, the boxes were full. The club’s leader, Sora, says the result is something she did not expect. “I thought people who ignored recycling would never change,” she says. “But when it is easy, they join us.” Now the club wants to find places where they can put more boxes.

qs.q: What did Sora learn from the project?
o: Shop owners dislike recycling boxes.
Batteries cannot be collected at school.
Posters help students remember to recycle.
Many people recycle when it is made easy.
qs.why: 쉬워지면 사람들이 동참한다는 점을 깨달았다고 했어요.

qs.q: Where was the second box placed?
o: Inside the library of Sora’s school
At the door of an electronics shop
On the wall next to the old posters
In the classroom where the club meets
qs.why: a shop owner whose store sells electronics ... a second box at his door라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence “Their latest project is a box that collects used batteries,” “that” refers to
o: the club
a box
the batteries
the classroom
qs.why: that의 선행사는 a box예요.

qs.q: What does the club want to do next?
o: Throw away the old posters on the walls
Ask Sora to step down as the club leader
Find more places for collection boxes
Stop holding meetings on Thursday afternoons
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 상자를 더 둘 장소를 찾고 싶다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word “ignored” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: looked at very carefully
talked about with joy
paid no attention to
fixed in a short time
qs.why: ignore는 관심을 주지 않는다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Day on the Island
items.text: June 12. Today we visited a beach where the sand was almost black. My brother, who is afraid of big waves, stayed near the rocks, but I walked into the water that felt surprisingly warm. Dad took a photo of a boy whose kite flew high above the beach. In the evening, we ate at a small restaurant where the owner gave us free tea. She told us about a trail that goes around the island and takes three days to walk. Mom said we should come back in autumn, when the weather is cooler.

qs.q: What kind of text is this passage?
o: A news report
A diary entry
A school rule
A travel advertisement
qs.why: 날짜로 시작하고 하루의 일을 일인칭으로 적은 일기예요.

qs.q: Why did the brother stay near the rocks?
o: He was looking for his kite.
He wanted to take photos for Dad.
He did not like the black sand.
He was afraid of big waves.
qs.why: who is afraid of big waves라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence “the water that felt surprisingly warm,” “that” refers to
o: the water
the beach
the sand
the rocks
qs.why: that은 앞의 the water를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does Mom want to come back in autumn?
o: The restaurant will give free tea.
The weather is cooler then.
The trail takes three days to walk.
The waves are bigger then.
qs.why: when the weather is cooler라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the owner of the restaurant tell the family about?
o: A beach with warm water
A boy with a kite
A long walking trail
A cooler season
qs.why: She told us about a trail that goes around the island라고 했어요.

items.title: The Music Festival
items.text: Our town holds a music festival every spring. It is an event that brings together people who play different kinds of instruments. This year, a group of teenagers whose band had practiced in a garage performed on the main stage. The singer, who had been nervous all week, forgot the first line of the song, but the audience, which had come to support them, sang it for her. Afterward, she said the moment she would never forget was the one when everyone sang together. The festival ends with a concert that anyone can join, so bring an instrument if you have one.

qs.q: What happened when the singer forgot the first line?
o: The band stopped the concert.
The audience sang it for her.
Another singer took her place.
The teenagers left the stage.
qs.why: the audience ... sang it for her라고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Teenagers should always practice their songs in garages.
Singers must learn every line well before a show.
The town’s festival is a place for sharing music.
Spring is the best season of the year for concerts.
qs.why: 마을 축제에서 사람들이 함께 음악을 나누는 모습이 글 전체의 중심이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence “the audience, which had come to support them,” “them” refers to
o: the teenagers in the band
the people who play instruments
the festival workers
the people in the garage
qs.why: them은 무대에서 공연한 십 대 밴드를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say “bring an instrument if you have one”?
o: Everyone must play a solo on the stage.
The festival sells instruments to visitors.
The band needs new members this spring.
Anyone can take part in the final concert.
qs.why: a concert that anyone can join이라고 했으니 누구나 참여할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did the singer probably feel before the show?
o: Nervous
Bored
Angry
Proud
qs.why: who had been nervous all week라고 했어요.

items.ex: Can you describe the person who took your bag?
items.exko: 네 가방을 가져간 사람을 묘사해 줄 수 있니?

items.ex: That is the reason why I called you.
A hammer is a tool that people use to hit nails.
items.exko: 망치는 사람들이 못을 박을 때 쓰는 도구예요.
